children.text: For the padding select of the element toolbar

All four pick sides with ⌘-click and set every side picked with one step of the scale. They differ in how much of the box they draw and whether margin is part of it. Today a page has padding and a parent's gap, no margin: only B adds it.
The box, padding only. The sides are wide bands around the content, so they are easy to hit and to ⌘-click; the value sits in the band. The gap stays its own select, next to it in the toolbar.
Reads like the devtools without a ring that is not really there
Big targets, the picked sides are obvious
Takes more room than the list it replaces
Margin, if it comes later, needs a second ring
The devtools box, whole: margin in orange around the padding in green, both editable, picked together across the rings. The select becomes spacing and its value says both.
Exactly the mental model of the devtools and of CSS
One place for all spacing around an element
Margin and gap both push siblings apart: two ways to say one thing
Needs a margin field on every node (the same shape as padding), written as m-*, mx-*, ml-*.

As Figma and the inspector do it: X and Y, opened out to four sides with the corner button. Each field is a select of the scale, scrubbed by dragging it; ⌘-click picks several fields and the list sets them all.
click to pick several fields · drag a field to scrub

children.text: Smallest; the same control as the inspector in Design mode
Values are typed or scrubbed without looking for a band
No picture: which side is which rests on the arrow icons
Less like the devtools you asked for

The list that is there today, with a side picker above it: click an edge of the square or one of all, x, y, t, r, b, l, ⌘-click for several. The list then writes the class for those sides, and marks where each picked side is now.
The classes read as Tailwind writes them: px, pt, pl
The values of the sides are not all visible at once
The picker is small to hit
